title: Auto-BACKLOG tasks after repeated empty-progress refusals
description: Objective: a task released >=3 times within 24h with zero step progress since claim is routed to BACKLOG (human-gated) instead of thrashing the scheduler — mirrors the blocked-timeout park precedent. Deliverable: refusal counting in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/releaseTask.ts + settings.refusalCascadeAutoBacklog opt-out (default on). NOT in scope: changing nextStatusForRelease for normal releases. Spec: item #4 in tag archive/governance-plane-v2. Verification command: npx vitest run src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts
definitionOfDone: Third empty-progress release inside 24h routes the task to BACKLOG with an explanatory system message
Releases WITH step progress never count toward the cascade
settings.refusalCascadeAutoBacklog: false disables the routing; setting validated and documented

implementationPlan.description: Extend `releaseTask.test.ts` first with deterministic, mutation-resistant coverage using fixed system time and seeded newest-first `priorHandoffs`. Assert that two qualifying empty-progress handoffs plus a third assigned-worker release inside the inclusive 24-hour window yields `status: 'BACKLOG'`, `cascadeTriggered: true`, a cleared assignee/IDLE prior worker, preserved handoff history, and a governor system message naming the task, threshold, and human-triage action. Add negative cases proving a current handoff that reports concrete work, fewer than three qualifying releases, malformed/expired timestamps, a release without a handoff, and `refusalCascadeAutoBacklog: false` all preserve normal `nextStatusForRelease` routing. Exercise `StateManager.updateSettings` in the same required test target to prove booleans persist, non-booleans fail through existing error handling without partial mutation, and the default-on behavior applies when the key is absent.
implementationPlan.note: Added `refusal cascade → BACKLOG` suite (17 cases) to releaseTask.test.ts: fixed system time (Date-only fake timers) + seeded newest-first priorHandoffs. Positives: third empty-progress release parks to BACKLOG with cascadeTriggered, cleared assignee, IDLE prior worker, preserved 3-entry history, untouched reopenCount/reopenReason, governor message naming task/threshold/human triage; inclusive 24h boundary; explicit true. Negatives: just-outside-window, malformed + future releasedAt, current handoff with real work, prior handoffs with real work, only-second refusal, no-handoff release, opt-out false, already-unassigned repair path, terminal DONE with stale assignee. Settings: updateSettings persists explicit false to disk, non-boolean rejects with no partial mutation, absent key defaults on. RED verified: `npx vitest run src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts` → 6 failed | 24 passed (30); failures are exactly the missing feature (status WORKING vs BACKLOG, undefined cascadeTriggered, "is not a supported project setting field").

implementationPlan.description: Add the backward-compatible optional setting `refusalCascadeAutoBacklog?: boolean` to daemon `ProjectSettings`. Whitelist it in `StateManager.validateSettingsUpdate` and validate supplied values with `validateBooleanValue`; leave omission distinct from `false` so old project files default on at the release decision while an explicit false survives partial settings updates. Do not add unrelated task state or repurpose QA-owned `reopenCount`/`reopenReason`.
implementationPlan.note: Added optional `refusalCascadeAutoBacklog?: boolean` to ProjectSettings (schema.ts) documenting default-on-by-absence, plus the whitelist entry and validateBooleanValue branch in StateManager.validateSettingsUpdate. Value is stored as supplied so absence stays distinct from explicit false; validation throws before `next` is committed, so a bad value cannot partially mutate settings. `npx vitest run src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts` → 4 failed | 26 passed (30): the 2 settings-validation failures are gone, remaining 4 are the not-yet-implemented cascade.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the bounded refusal classifier and cascade in `releaseTask.ts`, adapting the archived item to current-main release semantics rather than copying it. Define an empty-progress handoff conservatively from the persisted structured `whatIsDone` field (trimmed/case-folded exact `nothing`/`none`/`n/a`/`na`, plus `nothing…` or `no progress…` prefixes); missing handoffs and any positive work description do not count. On a real assigned-worker release only, prepend the current handoff as today, scan the capped handoff history for finite `releasedAt` timestamps within 24 hours of the current release, and when the third qualifying release is reached and `state.project.settings.refusalCascadeAutoBacklog !== false`, override only that release's normal computed status to `BACKLOG`. Keep ordinary releases routed by the unchanged `nextStatusForRelease`, keep DONE/ARCHIVED and already-unassigned behavior unchanged, and return `cascadeTriggered: true` only on the triggering call.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented in releaseTask.ts: `isEmptyProgressHandoff` (trimmed/case-folded exact nothing|none|n/a|na plus /^nothing\b/ and /^no progress\b/; empty or non-string whatIsDone means unknown and does NOT count) and `countRecentRefusals` (Array.isArray guard for hand-edited .moe/, skips non-finite/out-of-window/future releasedAt, bounded by the existing 20-entry cap, pure in-memory). In the assigned-worker branch only, after the handoff is prepended, the cascade computes `nextStatusForRelease(task, 'park')` — reusing the existing blocked-timeout park routing rather than hardcoding BACKLOG, so DONE/ARCHIVED/AWAITING_APPROVAL stay put and nextStatusForRelease is unchanged — and overrides updates.status only when park resolves to BACKLOG, the task is not already BACKLOG, settings.refusalCascadeAutoBacklog !== false, and the count reaches 3. Response gains `cascadeTriggered: true` + an explanatory message on the triggering call only; reopenCount/reopenReason untouched. `npx vitest run src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts` → 1 failed | 29 passed (30); the one failure is the step-4 governor notification assertion.

implementationPlan.description: Add the explanatory cascade notification and update the tool description without weakening release error handling. After the task/worker updates succeed, post a dedicated best-effort message to `#governors` stating that the task was parked after three empty-progress releases in 24 hours and requires human reprioritization; swallow notification failures exactly like existing release broadcasts so chat cannot roll back or fail the release. Keep the scan bounded by the existing 20-handoff cap, perform no filesystem/network work under `StateManager.runExclusive`, and do not modify `nextStatusForRelease` or other automatic/deregister release paths.
implementationPlan.note: Added the dedicated #governors cascade post after the task/worker writes land, wrapped in the same try/catch-and-swallow as the existing release broadcasts so a chat failure can neither fail nor roll back a durable release. Message names the task id + title, the 3-in-24h threshold, why requeueing would thrash, and the human un-park path (moe.set_task_status → PLANNING/WORKING). Updated the moe.release_task tool description with the one exception to in-place routing, the whatIsDone qualification, cascadeTriggered, and the opt-out setting. No changes to nextStatusForRelease, deregister, or the stale-worker sweep; the refusal scan is in-memory over the existing 20-entry cap with no I/O under runExclusive. `npx vitest run src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts` → 30 passed (30).

Also added the cascade line to the governor auto-push signal catalogue.

implementationPlan.description: Perform an adversarial self-review before verification: check the threshold is exactly the third qualifying release; the window comparison is deterministic and ignores invalid/future/out-of-window timestamps; explicit false is not lost to defaulting; positive-progress and handoff-less releases never count; already-unassigned retries cannot manufacture refusals; normal WORKING→WORKING/complete→REVIEW routing and terminal no-ops are unchanged; the worker is still idled when a cascade parks the task; QA reopen counters are untouched; message-post failures remain non-fatal; and the bounded scan adds no long synchronous work under the state mutex. Correct any issue found before the final run.
implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review of the diff, item by item. Verified: threshold is exactly the 3rd (count includes the just-prepended current note, which always survives the slice(0,20) cap since it sits at index 0; 2 priors + current parks, 1 prior + current does not). Window is deterministic — nowMs is Date.parse of the note's own releasedAt, not a second wall-clock read, so the current release is always inside its own window and a clock move between stamping and mutex entry cannot change the verdict; non-finite, future, and pre-cutoff timestamps are skipped. Opt-out reads `state.project?.settings?.refusalCascadeAutoBacklog !== false` (optional chaining on settings per the hand-editable-project.json gotcha), so explicit false survives and absence stays enabled. Positive-progress and handoff-less releases cannot qualify (cascadeEligible requires a non-null handoff that classifies empty). Already-unassigned repair calls return before the cascade block. nextStatusForRelease is untouched — the park reuses its existing 'park' context, so DONE/ARCHIVED/AWAITING_APPROVAL are inert, and an extra `task.status !== 'BACKLOG'` guard stops a re-park claiming cascadeTriggered. Worker is still idled (unconditional block after updateTask); reopenCount/reopenReason untouched; both chat posts are swallow-on-error and land after the durable writes; the scan is O(20) in-memory with no I/O under runExclusive; the two regexes are anchored with no quantifiers (no ReDoS) over a 4000-char-clamped field. Checked callers: the only non-agent caller is WebSocketServer RELEASE_TASK (board button), which passes no handoffNote and therefore can never park a task. Accepted-and-noted residual risk: a proxy-retried release could prepend a duplicate empty-progress note via the already-unassigned repair path, which could contribute one extra qualifying entry; deduping was rejected because any key (releasedBy or releasedAt) either hides genuine repeat refusals from the same resumed workerId or is defeated by ms-apart timestamps, and the false-positive cost is one human set_task_status. Evidence: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, and the full daemon suite `npx vitest run` → 49 files / 773 tests passed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The archived tag's item #4 was inspected as a behavioral spec. Its reuse of newest-first `priorHandoffs`, 24-hour threshold, default-on boolean, and conservative `whatIsDone` classifier is appropriate because current `release_task` already persists the only release-scoped progress evidence there. Adding a claim-time baseline or new refusal-history task field was rejected: it would expand into claim/schema migration work despite the task explicitly scoping counting to `releaseTask.ts`. Counting any task with zero globally completed steps was rejected because a later claimant can make zero new progress on a partially completed task. Hard-coding all releases to BACKLOG or changing `nextStatusForRelease` was rejected by the task rail. The archived updates to `reopenCount`/`reopenReason` are deliberately not carried forward because current main uses those fields for QA rejection caps and metrics.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Current `releaseTaskTool` validates handoffs before the mutex, prepends them to `priorHandoffs` (capped at 20), computes assigned-release status with `nextStatusForRelease`, updates the former worker to IDLE, and treats channel posts as best-effort. DONE/ARCHIVED unassigned releases are strict no-ops; already-unassigned releases have a separate repair/handoff path and should not count as new claim refusals. `HandoffNote` already provides `whatIsDone`, `releasedAt`, and `releasedBy`, so no new task/history schema is needed. `ProjectSettings` is in `types/schema.ts`; `validateSettingsUpdate` already exposes `validateBooleanValue`. The existing `docs/MCP_SERVER.md` release contract currently says only humans/blocked-timeout can park tasks, so it must be corrected alongside the two epic-required settings docs.
planningNotes.risks: The largest semantic risk is conflating no progress on the current claim with no completed steps over the task lifetime; using the release handoff avoids that and preserves partially completed tasks. Other risks are counting duplicate already-unassigned releases, treating missing handoffs as proof of no progress, off-by-one/window flakiness, using a truthy default that ignores explicit false, corrupting QA reopen counters by copying stale archived code, or letting a governor-channel failure fail a successful release. Tests should freeze time and assert exact status/response/message/state outcomes.
